reviews.title: Good, but not worth the price for full version.
reviews.text: So I got this game a while back, loved playing it. Reminded me of RuneScape a lot which I think is the point. Easy to understand and go about it as an idle game. All skills were open and no restrictions. However, when I opened it up today I noticed there is now a pay wall to most of the content. So all the work I put into skills are now blocked, some even maxed out but now unless I pay 10$ I can’t even view it. Of combat skills you can use only 4 of the 8. Attack, Strength, Defense, and Hitpoints. The blocked skills are ranged, magic, prayer, and slayer. These skills provide a lot of flexibility to combat and can make fights easier or more rewarding. Plus slayer unlocked new areas for you to fight in for better loot so it knocks out 14 additional zones you could choose from. For non-combat skills you can only use 6 of the 16: woodcutting,fishing,fire making,cooking, mining,and smithing.

reviews.title: a whole different tier of idle games
reviews.text: The only thing this game is missing is an in-game tutorial, which I learned is currently being developed after checking the development roadmap. This game will take a few minutes and maybe an hour to learn, but is very, very well worth it. If you don’t like in-depth games don’t waste your time downloading it. I recommend starting a regular account and once exploring a little, create a second account in adventure mode to use when not active on your main account. The wiki is extremely useful, and has a beginner guide to help you understand the game. Start with fishing or woodcutting if you have no idea what to do!

reviews.title: 5* for gameplay but 3* because of shady marketing
reviews.text: I’ve been playing Melvor daily for about 2 months now. Originally bought it on my PC through Steam. Then downloaded it on my phone to level skills when I wasn’t on pc. No complaints, very addictive. Then I get on today to train skills I’ve been training for weeks only to be told I’m in the “Demo Mode” and I’m locked out of skills I’ve been training (some of which I have gotten to 99 just on my phone) and I have to pay $10 to unlock them. Yet I already own the game on steam. Not sure how you can let people download for feee with no paywall and not mention anything about it being a demo then locking them out of parts of the game they’ve been playing. Probably won’t be playing much at all now as I don’t play it on pc much since mobile was way more convenient. If I’m going to play on my PC I’m going to be playing the real OSRS. reviews.title: RuneScape idle
reviews.text: I’ve had this game for a few days now and am enjoying it a lot. I tend to play an idle for about a week and get bored and delete it. This will be a different story though. I use to heavily play RuneScape back in the day (from 2003-present) with the last couple of years not having time sitting down to play due to being an adult. This brought a ton of nostalgia and is very easy to set a skill and essentially afk it for a few hours to come back and check on the progress. I upgraded to the premium to get all the skills. I am running 5 different characters having them all focus on different skills to see how they all work. Most of the skills are identical to RS in progress/tiers. I have not dived into combat yet though. Thanks Jagex for another fantastic game!

reviews.text: (For people with issues with ads are you sure you can’t just tap an x to close it? Because I can) I found this while I was trying out the new rs3 skill finally. This idle game kept me from getting back into my rs addiction with a fun less time consuming but still addictive alternative. It’s got way more depth in it than most idle games. The app is a bit buggy. For example, sometimes I need to open the app twice to get it to load. Sometimes offline progress doesn’t work super well. I tend to have random logs in my bank. That being said it’s an amazing concept and I suggest support the maker since they’re working hard to update it constantly. Great for rs nerds and great for anyone else tbh.

reviews.title: Fun distraction.
reviews.text: I have “played” a number of clicker games such as cookie clicker and clicker hero’s.  I think is game hits a sweet spot.   It is a incremental game that proceeds while you are off line, but the whole time you are building a character up to eventually be able to raid dungeons.   Like a good rpg,  the way you go about this is variable.  Do you grow trees?  Rob various npc’s?  Fish. Cook?  The list goes on.   I like to pretend I am guiding this character through his adventures.   I think I spent about 5 bucks for this game, a real bargain!  And content is still coming out.  Oh, and the globin raid is a great way to see some of the goodies that your character will eventually acquire.  Well designed game!  Now, some mild sound effects and a riveting music score and I think this game could be a classic.

It’s super easy and satisfying. The only things I would love to see is maybe somehow incorporate a avatar doing the skills. This would give it a new perspective for example the character fishing, mining, combat, etc. It would be cool to customize the character too and see the armor and gear. Another feature would be awesome to put a few of the songs from RuneScape. I love the nostalgia feeling of listening to Garden, Wander, Dream and the other great songs you guys made. Thank you for making this game so easy to play and enjoy. I feel you can definitely get $10 worth out of it.

reviews.title: Best Idle Game Ever
reviews.text: First of all, I used to be an old RuneScape player years ago.  I only recently found out about this game and absolutely enjoy it.  It takes the best stuff from RuneScape and removes the worst, such as no more competing for resources and you no longer have to waste time traveling.  Also, it’s like playing RuneScape with a bot, like telling it to mine an ore until you tell it to stop.  Sure, not all the skills are available in the f2p but you can do everything in those free skills unlike RuneScape.  I’m sorry but if your complaining about the one time $10 fee to open the rest of the game, then you’re an idiot.  That’s a bargain compared to RuneScape.  Once I get done with most of the f2p skills, I plan on paying for the rest.  Fantastic game!

Love the gameplay and content of the new update, but the app freezes constantly now. It will often hang when opening a new file from the cloud and keep you locked at the AFK results screen until you force close. There’s also an extremely frustrating bug where you open the side menu by sliding it out from the left and try to scroll around on it, but instead it keeps scrolling whatever screen is underneath it. This allows you to interact with the screen underneath as well, up to and including unchecking a box that allows you to eat food automatically on your hardcore character… glad I caught that one before your broken game deleted a few months worth of my effort.

Great game all around, but the lack of polish on this update really hurts the experience if you play mostly on mobile.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: I’ve been playing this game ever since it was first available. Throughout its beta, you had access to everything in the game. I had gotten 99’s in almost everything and put the game down for awhile. Then it released and I decided to check out all the cool new things. It’s awesome I still have my same character, but half the skills are now locked unless you pay for it. All the skills I need to work on are now locked. I was a range pure as well, guess what is also locked, RANGED COMBAT. The character I have spent many many months on is now useless and I can’t proceed to do anything else since what I do have unlocked is already 99. I loved this game but I can’t play it after knowing I either need to start over or pay $10 just to unlock all the stuff I had access to before for a long time.

reviews.title: Best ever idle game ever
reviews.text: I literally play this version only i left RS3 for this game.  I want to see a GE marketplace in game but the game is still newerish as of writing but honestly this is hands diwn the best version of runescape. Im a very loyal day one premium player. Theres so much to do and so much to progress but so fun, addicting and worth it. Graphics are simple but very smooth and gameplay and functions are always operational and up to date. Thx devs. 😉 im a long term player and highly recommend this to anyone looking for a great simple mobile full on idle mmorpg game.  Player base has been growing alot too so i cant wait for competitive pvp and GE to come out. What an incredible game. Ty so much for this. Been waiting years for a idle and mobile RS version

reviews.title: Great idle game to download
reviews.text:
This is a great game through and through. I have been playing the game since it’s early days and it’s only been getting better. Through the addition of skills and reworking skills so they can be more enjoyable, I think the developers are on a very good path with this game. If you like progression and climbing tiers then this is the game you want to play. 

One small minor thing I would like added to the game is a tier list added to the combat skill tabs. In the skilling tabs, there tier list is shown as the medallion in the bottom right corner. The combat one doesn’t seem to have that and it’s hard to find that list. Besides that this is a great game and I will continue to support.

reviews.title: Uneducated Reviewers
reviews.text: Plenty of people in the comments (like the “top helpful comment”) crying about there being a paid expansion alongside a $10 game. There are NO microtransactions. There is enough content in the single game to keep you busy for months if not a year. I still haven’t bothered buying it because I’ve wanted to level up my other stats first— and now Melvor Idle 2 is coming. Idk how these people’s vote counts the same as mine. Clearly they’re not crying when big corporate games cost $60 and force microtransactions, but God forbid developers try to support their game with a reasonable DLC expansion. Was no one around during Xbox or PS3 days? $15 map packs on CoD??? Exactly. Now hush and enjoy the game

reviews.title: Amazing Idle! Well worth the money
reviews.text: The new expansion just dropped today and honestly for the time I’ve put in, with only a little bit of money, its the best bang of the buck I’ve ever purchased! I couldn’t be happier supporting this team and all the hard work they put into this. Great game and great content for those of use who used to play RuneScape back in the day. The team constantly does updates based on feedback and with the new expansion it’s as if its a brand new game again. I know I’ll be playing for a long time into the future. With a busy life this is the perfect pick it up in the morning and check it before going to bed type of idle! Thanks again for the fun!

reviews.title: Amazing with a major flaw
reviews.text:
First the good, this is by far one of the best mobile games I’ve ever played. The game doesn’t try to squeeze your wallet dry like other mobile games. You pay for the game and expansions and that’s it. Obviously, it is heavily inspired by RuneScape but it still has a uniqueness to it. If you like idle games and you’ve enjoyed RuneScape at any point, you will probably like this game. 

Now the bad. I have stopped playing this game because of a skill called Township. It essentially devalues coins and resources so much that I don’t really want to play anymore. Before, I used to spend time gathering resources to Smith or Fletch or whatever, in order to make money to buy upgrades and stuff. Now with Township, I have billions of gold and tens of thousands of each resource. There’s basically nothing for me to chase anymore other than gear. 

Another thing that isn’t ideal. When you get to the h

reviews.title: Best idle game you will ever play
reviews.text:
Got this game because I’m a fan of RuneScape and hearing it was based off it made me hooked, I spent days ignoring real life problems and situations and friends to play this game. My friends say I have a problem but frankly I think they have a problem for not playing this game and I think you have a problem too for not playing this game. Here’s a few good reasons. 

The game is free, you get the idle incremental gameplay you expect from an idle game but with updates here and there. 

The full price is a one time payment and you get so much from it that if you’re casually playing it, you can easily spend a year playing. 

The full game comes with 2 other game modes if you think you’re up for strategic idling. 

You don’t have to play and be limited by a small timer and it stops, this game gives you 18 hours of idle before it stops you. That’s a lot of idle.

Anyway I have to go, the wife

reviews.title: Fantastic.
reviews.text:
Great game. Takes the completionist appeal of “one specific game” and turns it into a fun idler. 

TL;DR I’m loving the game. But the layouts have some hierarchy and consistency issues which make it hard to know what I’m looking at and how to start a skill.  

Some suggestions: 

Make “start/stop action” more consistent across every skill. Right now it’s a little scattered on where you actually tap to start a skill. Maybe just a button right on top. 

The combat screen is a little scattered, and many of the different combat modes just bring you to the same screen, leaving you curious if the button worked or if it’s bugged. I understand why it’s laid out that way, but I would explore different ways of phrasing buttons or menus. Maybe a “combat” button in the menu with a description of “trains STR/DEF/etc” on the page instead of having each separate STR/DEF/etc button bring you to the same

reviews.title: Best idle game out there
reviews.text: I have played this game over a year and a half and have 3 different saves, a normal a adventure and a hardcore character. I have yet to reach 100% completion on my normal character. Once you get going you can just afk every 18 hours if that’s what you want till you hit offline cap. Coming back after 18 hours if you do choose that way you just pick up where you left off. Developers are constantly updating the game over and open massive expansions planned for a 10 dollar game if you choose to upgrade it is highly recommended if you enjoying feeling you are progressing every day you will always get something done.

reviews.title: “Full version”
reviews.text: I had really loved this game. I had played it before the Jagex Team (who runs RuneScape) bought them out and played it on the off hours when I wasn’t busy and let it build up my skills when I was at work. The game was FANTASIC… it kept my skills and didn’t lock the others… but after I went to bed the other day and reopened it this morning (Juneteenth) and for some reason my account got “locked” behind the “free” version… and honestly, I’m just done. — no point supporting a game that was INTENTIONALLY free and get locked behind something that originally had built up… I get this was based off the “RuneScape” game… but this is just terrible changes from the new developer (jagex) — I’m at the point of deciding to uninstall… I am NOT a fan of these new changes. I really don’t like when game devs do this crap just to gain a quick buck. It was a fun journey Melvor… but this “adventure” ends her

reviews.title: Hands down the best idle game I’ve ever played
reviews.text: I don’t normally write reviews but these devs deserve some recognition. Not only is this the best idle game I’ve ever played it’s the best mobile game. A game I can play for a couple minutes here and there, but with enough depth to keep me playing for months. I was hesitant at first because every mobile game I’ve played apart from premium triple A games that you pay 10+ dollars for have had a predatory business model. This game however goes back to the roots of what game making should be. If you put out a quality game it will do well and be received by others. I would pay to support these people any day. Thank you for the well made, well thought out game.

reviews.title: I never write reviews. This made me write one.
reviews.text: I realize I’m a weird one - but this game captures something I loved about games like RuneScape. A million skills to train and each affects different things you do in the game. You learn as you go - it’s way more fun to just start chopping some wood at first and leave it alone for a while - racking up coal in the fire making skill from burning logs - then feeling rewarded when all that coal gets put to good use smelting. It’s a cool eco system to just check in on a few times a day. Fights have been challenging so far - reminding me of the skills and materials I’ve neglected. I don’t have another game like this one, and I’ve really enjoyed it.

reviews.title: Enjoy playing few minor things that need fixing
reviews.text:
Tbh I was skeptical of this game…. My friend told me about it and I said the hype with this game will die out within 2 weeks time I’m not going to be spending $10 knowing that… after about a day he told me it’s available as a mobile app for free next thing you know I bought the full version… it beats spending $70 a year to play osrs… if you like the concept of grinding and achieving things and unlocking new things while continually progressing this is your game! I am throughly enjoying the game currently but there are a few things that need fixing as I learn more I will update this review as well.

1. When killing an npc say chickens for example the loot at the bottom allows you to collect 100 killed npc loot at a time. The problem with it is that bones are stackable but when you look at feathers and chicken parts they are registering per kill rather than just stacking on top of one anot

reviews.title: Almost all good
reviews.text: I rarely ever write reviews but I’m writing this in hopes that the creators see a but of advice. I love the game and I especially appreciate that the game can be on the computer. My only gripe has to do with any skill that deduct health. For whatever reason, if I try to idle Attack, Thieving, Defense, etc, the second that I click off to let it run it stops the progress. This is the same if I switch tabs for a second on the browser. Another thing is I think it might be best to come up with your own names for items and materials since they’re so close to RuneScape that the game might get in trouble in the future. Thanks and keep up the good work!

reviews.title: Your not RuneScape.
reviews.text:
I loved this game. Still do. I think it is a very interesting idea and take for an idle/text based RuneScape. It’s obvious inspirations. All good and dandy. But what I mean, 10 dollars for premium? That is straight hog wash. Sincerely a bad move. Introducing an ad free option, sure. But you made a different move. I’ll repeat. You are not RuneScape. You took the inspiration too far. Now copying their member and non member format. Nah. You guys lost me. 10 bucks Is not much. But this game is not worth 10 dollars, at least in the way you are going about it. And sense you know, your road map seems to have been abandoned. 

** It is obvious to see now that this was a cash grab from the start. You started slow, built people’s interest and time. Then boom, pay for access to practically the whole game. Let’s hope you don’t make more then a purchase. You sir, are a degenerate scam artist.

reviews.title: 10$ to play way was originally free
reviews.text: I had started playing Melvor idle when it was pretty early in development and enjoying the RuneScape inspired aspects of the game and how many different things I could level and earn. I had stopped playing for a while but saw that this game was eventually picked up by Jagex. I was honestly pretty happy for the original developer(s). But now that I logged back in hoping to continue a lost and forgotten grind to see that  everything I had worked hard for previously is now locked behind a pay wall is B.S. I’m really disappointed with the direction this game took I had never got the chance to play RuneScape as a premium member as a kid so I thought I could see what I missed out on. Guess not. Guess I’ll uninstall and go back to Cookie Clicker or AdVenture Capitalist

reviews.title: A TRUE Idle game!
reviews.text:
I downloaded Melvor Idle yesterday and I am loving it! So many skills to master and you are always making progress! 
The user interface is very friendly and there are plenty of non-intrusive hints and tutorials to help you along the way! 
The ONLY In-App purchase is to remove the ads. The ads are non-intrusive and I hardly noticed them, however I did pay to remove the ads because I greatly appreciate all the time and care put into creating this elegant and rewarding idle game experience!

I restarted the app and I was able to create an account using the “Sign into Melvor Cloud” button above the character select and every

reviews.title: Update! 5 star
reviews.text: Bugs were fixed and I can login! Thanks so much to the person/team who fixed this! I’m back to the grind! Love this game! It is $10 which people are complaining about…I chose to spend the $10 because I believe I’m getting WAAAY more than $10 out of my time spent on the game. I spend about 1 hour every day on the game…which over 30 days of constant play makes it very much worth it for me. Also…just a heads up…I strongly recommend if you’re gonna take this game somewhat serious and have fun doing combat…you’ll need to spend the $10 potions are insanely beneficial

reviews.title: Fun but too expensive
reviews.text: I’ve played the free version for a while and it’s very clearly a fun game, but it’s frustrating how you either choose between less than half of the game’s total content or paying $10 for a mobile idle game. I understand the devs need some kind of revenue, but please, please consider lowering the price. I guarantee that lots of people like me like the game enough to justify buying it but are scared off by the price tag. If you lower it then more people will buy. Most mobile games are $5 which seems like a very reasonable price to me. The most popular exception is minecraft, but then again there’s so much content in minecraft that the price tag is justified. The game is good, but put simply it isn’t $10 good.

reviews.title: Pay to play $$$
reviews.text: This was one of the best idle games ever made. Had everything a RuneScape fan is looking for. The format and functionality of the game was on point, still is honestly. But since the newest update over half of all skills are now locked. You can not truly play this game anymore unless you can afford to pay. They are a “business” after all I suppose but I figured that’s why there were ads in the game and the option to pay to remove them, but ultimately you could still play.. not anymore. You MUST pay to play now :(… just deleting this game now… was fun and I hope the creator makes the money he/she is looking for, just it will not be made from me. Got to make that money with the forced ads and I can not contribute anything more. Sad I wasted so many hours on this game just for this to happen :/…

reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.text:
I’ve been playing for about a week now and just love the progression of all the systems. I pretty much only play idle games and this is at the top of my list.

I know it’s still being worked on but a few suggestions, I’ve been having trouble seeing what prayers do because the info blip only stays a split second before it activates a prayer. The only other thing is when you click gear in the gear menu and it unequips it, usually it’s not a problem but when it is, is when I’m trying to see stats before switching gear. 

Other then those two things I adore it I’ll be continuing to play and see what you guys do with it!

reviews.title: Looks Can Be Deceiving
reviews.text:
Seemed like a clean game with lots of numbers to raise and tasks to complete. Right up my alley! What I got instead was a janky user experience and lots of different design decisions from screen to screen adding up to a game that, while admittedly incomplete, feels like it has no idea what it is trying to be. Forgivable, I thought, since it’s in alpha. 

On second launch I was shown ugly ads at the top and bottom of the page. So much for a clean interface! You want to crowdsource alpha testing AND show ads to your users? Pretty shameful. There are tactful ways to display ads and tactful ways to release a game before completion. The developer of this did neither. 

The craziest part is that based on the App Store screenshots alone I would have paid for this app. The world needs a clean idle game with lots of levers to pull and buttons to push. Unfortunately, this is not that game.

reviews.title: Probably the finest idle game ever produced
reviews.text: I have played many idle games before. None have been able to surpass the variety of content that this game offers. Though it does come with a price for the full release, it is well worth the $10 for the base game. I’ve yet to reach the expansion content, but from what I’ve seen from goblin raid and the new town keeping skill, I’m sure it won’t disappoint. They also have mod support directly with a mod manager directly in the UI. And to top off they provide regular content and bug fixes through updates; all without a single micro transaction.

reviews.title: Very solid game
reviews.text:
Honestly such a well put together game that feels like you're playing text-based old school runescape, but without the crazy grind that osrs requires.  

I'd love to see an update that implements interacting with items within your bank. i.e. If you tap on rune essence it brings up an additional option to go to the runecrafting screen so I don't have to click on menu to go scroll through runecrafting.  Same with hides within your bank to bring you to the crafting screen automatically.

Anyways, great game over all, I definitely recommend to give it a go!

reviews.title: Hands down best incremental game I’ve ever played
reviews.text:
I’ve played a lot of them... probably most of them. I haven’t had this much fun in a long time. I usually the guy that finds a “beginners guide” right away and follows that. I’m not doing that with this game and it’s making it exponentially more fun. Could I be more efficient? Probably... but I’m learning the game in my terms and I love it. Their wiki is also a great resource when you get confused which happens occasionally. But let me clarify that getting confused is a good thing. 

Shout out to the dev/s. Thanks for all the fun and I look forward to continue to support you. This game is seriously the best!

reviews.title: Is there better?
reviews.text:
Let me start with: The game didn’t ask me “How are you enjoying the game” like MANY other games do. It gets better. I almost never review games, but it doesn’t even give you pop up video ads... So I had to, and if you’re still not convinced the game is definitely worth downloading, this might convince you.. It’s basically the Idle version of RuneScape.. I haven’t put my phone down all day.. The only thing I would say needs help is me, putting my phone down for more than 20 seconds. Sorry for the long review. For anyone that didn’t read the whole thing: JUST DOWNLOAD IT. YOU’RE WELCOME.

MALCS, YOU ARE A GENIUS!

reviews.title: Fun Sometimes
reviews.text: This game in and of itself is pretty fun, and I can see that it has a lot of potential. I love that it has so many skills and that you can make multiple characters. If everything else worked well this game would absolutely have a 5/5. That being said my game crashes about 75% of the time, and it’s really frustrating. I’ll load into one of my two characters, switch to another tab (bank, skill, combat, etc.), and POOF it crashes and sends me to the main screen. The icing on this crap cake is sometimes when it crashes it will take whatever I was working on with it. (RIP 5k lobbies, countless rune essence, and 3k steel bars). As soon as developers can fix this bug, I will genuinely switch my rating to the five stars that this game deserves. Happy playing and good luck!

reviews.title: Great game
reviews.text:
I must admit, this is the 2nd time I downloaded the game. The first time I thought it was kinda dumb, there was no direction, I didn’t know what to do so I deleted it within 15 min. A few days later I gave it another try. I’m so glad I did! The depth and flexibility it so great. There’s a time for AFK, and things you need a more active game for. There’s no direct linear path, just a rough direction of what to do, just wonderful. 

I’d add some sort of explanation of what to do, though. There’s a wiki, sure, but I was lucky enough to give it a 2nd try. Who’s knows how many would not come back…

reviews.title: 'the' game for me
reviews.text: This game is heaven sent. I love it. I can fight all day and fish all night, all the while farming. OR I can do a multitude of other things, whatever my heart's desire. There are many skills to level up, many goals to obtain.. or not. I love carving my own path. This game fits to a tee. It's fun and it really stratches an itch. One of the biggest draws, I can maintain quality of life while playing. I can lay it down and let it cook or I can get lost in it for a couple hours, total freedom. I appreciate the simplicity, the complexity, the artwork and the subtle humor. Beautiful idle game. This here's a real gem boys.

reviews.title: Read this review.
reviews.text: i have to say that this is one of the best mobile games out there, and DEFINITELY the best idle game. Even though it is an idle game, there’s room for more active players, and I would say this game is the most fun when you check on it every 10-45 minutes. Of course in the early game its more fun to be more active. There is SO MUCH CONTENT in this game, even without the dlc. I got the dlc, but I’ve barely touched it (cuz I don’t understand most of it) and I’m still having the time of my life with this game. If you’re judging whether or not to get it, you should.

reviews.title: One of the best games I’ve ever played
reviews.text: It’s a must have for OSRS fans. A must have for idle game fans. A must have for anyone who appreciates amazing game design and progression. I’ve been playing this since it came out and years later, I still can’t get enough of it. I’m learning more about it all the time. It’s so easy to get started but takes a lot of time to really master. It’s deeper than you could possibly imagine when start and it never loses its charm. I can’t wait for the sequel but I still have SO much more to do in this one.

reviews.title: Great Game…Loads of Potential
reviews.text: While it makes RuneScape into an idle game it’s still a game within itself with tons to do and crazy amounts of potential if taken in the right direction. Would love to see some type of choose your own adventure type quests or something along those lines…One suggest though, It would help if we could change equipment from the actual equipment screen instead of only being able to equip items from the bank, this makes you take your attention away from battles.

reviews.title: Best Idle I’ve Played
reviews.text:
This is so true to RS, it makes you feel like your a lvl 3 starting in kumbridge 😁, the difference is the skills are much easier so you don’t have to spend hundreds or thousands of active hours. 

They have Barbarian Fishing which is an amazing way to get strength up without being in combat, which leads me to my next favorite thing so far which is their combat and slayer systems. As far as I know the combat is active (obviously) and the NPCs all have their drop tables readily available so you don’t have to go searching the Wiki, which they also have! 

10/10 would recommend

reviews.title: Are you addicted or do not have enough time for OSRS?
reviews.text:
I’ve played Runescape for several years on and off. Each time I started back up, I never could rationalize the time I spent on it. It often was a waste of my time and money. In an attempt to replace Runescape, I found this Melvor Idle and it has been great. Melvor Idle is a more satisfying and well-rounded experience. In other words, it fulfills the desire I have to play Runescape while allowing me to enjoy my real life! I wouldn’t necessarily say it is rewarding game, but I find it nostalgic and oddly satisfying.

Thank you developers for a well thought out and enjoyable game!

reviews.title: Hey love the game pls pls fix
reviews.text: So just wanna day this the first review I ever done for a game 😂 but this game is Grindy it’s an afk runescape and it’s free it’s a great idea but so for various items you can afk like right now I’m grinding smithing (mining and smithing for that gold ) but when I randomly check on it to see my loot or for it to mine something else or smith or any skill actually (that’s afk able ) it stops out of no where like idk what causes it to stop I don’t close the app or anything pls look into 🤙🏼 but only reason it’s getting a 4 star if you fix this I’ll give it a 5 star 🙂 but amazing game thanks for putting your hard work into this 🤙🏼

reviews.title: Great Game!
reviews.text: I love everything about it so far, the feel of the OsRs theme, & the style. Only thing that made me write a review was hoping dev’s see this and try to fix the shop as soon as possible. General upgrade don’t work at all right now unless it’s to purchase bank space. I can’t purchase multi-tree or any of the above. I cannot purchase a normal cooking fire for afk cooking. Just simple shop fixes would go a long long way in helping us continue to grind while this beautiful game comes out of Alpha. Keep up the great work, love it so far!

reviews.title: Ads ruin iOS app/webpage
reviews.text: Decided to try this game as I’ve been playing runescape for 15+ years on and off and that it’s also an app so I can take it with me.  Right off the bat, ads push the the dialogues and buttons off to the side of the screen so that I may not read or click them. Haven’t even created an account/character yet. Tried the webpage instead of the app and it does the same thing. I hate to give a 1 star review for a game that seems great, but ads literally ruin the experience. Not in the sense that “omg there’s ads” as I understand it’s a free game and the developers must make money somewhere. Until ads are either removed from the landing page/character creation screen or formatting is fixed you literally cannot read or play the game.

reviews.title: One of a Kind
reviews.text: Normally when I buy idle games, it's to pass the time on a boring day. I delete the game soon after, as I will probably never play it again. But with this game? Not so much. I got it thinking it was just another idle game, but this is so much more. I always seem to find myself coming back to it. I feel as though you've combined a good rpg with the idle system, like those who afk on Minecraft for extra items, but come back in an hour in order to play again with all their new treasures. Good job! I would highly recommend. Keep up the good work!!

reviews.title: Pretty Darn Good
reviews.text: Didn’t think I’d be into a game like this. An idle rpg isn’t usually something I go for, but I decided to try Melvor out anyways and boy oh boy was I glad I did. The art style is very nice for the eye to look at, there is lots of activities to level your character, and many different ways to build your character. After a couple of hours on the demo version I decided to buy the full game. Definitely gives a RuneScape vibe minus running to the bank and back, good for those who don’t have a lot of free time.

reviews.title: Perfect for...
reviews.text:
Those who don’t have the time to spend focusing and grinding on a game. That being said, you can absolutely grind if you like, and the interactive parts such as active healing, bonfire upkeep, etc., are fun in a single button pressing kinda way. 

I immediately got rid of the ads, and at $3, it was hardly a spend. Best choice I’ve made I think, and seeing as much of the game seems to be in development, I’m sure I’ll find more things to spend money on. Not much of a micro transaction guy, but this game has kept me hooked. GG, dev.

reviews.title: Constant ads in annoying places
reviews.text: Before their recent update I would have given this game a 5 stars because it is super fun and addicting, but the new update made it so you must have an internet connection to login so they can play ads on your screen (which is normally fine) but they place big ads on the bottom of your screen which you kind of need to see to view everything. And even worse the ads come back every 13-15 seconds (I counted). It turns into a constant nuisance. Developers need to make the ads smaller, less frequent, or just put the ads in different areas.

reviews.title: RuneScape Fans Rejoice!
reviews.text:
Growing up I absolutely loved playing RuneScape and I still do from time to time when I can make the time. With this though I don’t really need to make much time because most things I can do in the background. 
All around a great game and certainly makes me want to find more time for actual RuneScape, not many great games out these days on either phone or console/PC so this certainly lights that fire for RuneScape for me and keeps me occupied when I’m out and about. 
Amazing game and can’t wait for more updates and content!!

reviews.title: Was much much better.
reviews.text: I used to play this game a while ago maybe like a year or so. When I saw this game on my new phone I almost instantly download it. The entire game used to be free to play. However NOW more then half of the skills are locked behind an absolutely absurd $10 purchase. The tutorial shows you some skills that aren’t even available on the free version. Immediately after I finished the tutorial I looked at the skills and then uninstalled the game. Im so disappointed that this game became nothing more then a cash grab. I used to play this for hours on end. Now I’m not going to be playing at all.

reviews.title: Alpha was great. Beta lock down?
reviews.text: This game was so much fun! As someone who enjoys RuneScape so much and not having all the time to play it as before, this was perfect. I get the same feel of progression with less work. But when they decided to move to Beta and add the “premium” option, locking already accessible features and skills behind a paywall, I was shocked! Then I see if you have a cloud account you get them for free. But even after linking the account, there’s no way for that to be selected and unlocked. It remains locked away from the player. You get a 2 because of the enjoyment in Alpha and lost the other 3 because of a wall you put between me and the game.

reviews.title: Went from free to $$$$
reviews.text: I started playing this game a week before they switched from the completely free version to the paid version. It was worth the download and then a week later everything costed real money. As everyone probably already knows this game is the even idler version of RuneScape. If you’ve ever played RuneScape then you know that there’s a lot more content if you pay for the membership. However limiting the F2P RuneScape is, there still a lot of things that you are able to do without being a member. That said, this idle RS ripoff now makes you pay just for being idle. You can’t even train range, magic, or prayer without paying for it. It’s been deleted from my phone. Good luck gaining new players.

reviews.title: Alpha players
reviews.text: For the people that have played since the alpha versions 0.1-0.9 etc will we get the dlc for free? We have been playing since the beginning and it would be only fair we get the dlc free. If we have to pay, you may loose a lot of potential and current players. If we do get the dlc we(I)appreciate it. Hope to have access to it all. Also checked and my account is premium so can I assume my account would get the dlc? An answer would be appreciated as other alpha/premium account players may like to see the answer as well.

reviews.title: Fun game
reviews.text:
Game is very fun. Not a fast paced game but very intricate once you start linking items from one skill to another. just like RuneScape but you start the action and let it go. Check back in a bit and see what you’ve earned. Very helpful wiki guide online so very easy to navigate

Free version locks a good amount of the skills that are very necessary, so buying the game is highly recommended. Downloaded two years so still playing. DLC is cool though but not really that necessary until very late game

reviews.title: Fantastic game
reviews.text:
Just in general it’s a great game. In the idle genre it stands head and shoulders above the vast majority of idle games with one or two exceptions. The devs deserve the highest praise for the exceptional game that they’ve created. I am especially glad that they have allowed for continued progress across PC and mobile. I am at about 75% completion at the time of writing and I will without a doubt purchase the expansion with hopes of many more to come. Congratulations devs on your great game.

P.S. thanks for not gathering unnecessary data from users.

reviews.title: Old School Runescape Fan
reviews.text: I played RuneScape for years and this brings back great memories. I LOVE how this is turned into an idle game. So far I’m enjoying how everything works and being able to actually idle my skills while I’m not on it. Im addicted to it just like I was with RuneScape. It’s also not pay to win like most mobile games out there. I’m curious though to see how it would work if you could trade/sell/interact with other players. I completely recommend this game to any one who likes to just casual play, idle play, and RuneScape fans.

reviews.title: Excellent, but for a few things
reviews.text:
I’ve been playing about two days now. The game appears to still be in beta or even alpha, but it’s coming together very nicely. 

Devs: We have to talk about inventory space. It runs out far too quickly and at the beginning I don’t know what I need to keep and what I don’t. Inventory should be much higher to start and more inventory space should be purchasable in blocks, not in single spaces. 

The only other thing I want to ask about is making the magic system clearer. I have a staff equipped, but I’m still attacking guys with melee. I love the game. Excellent work!!

reviews.title: Big Fan!
reviews.text:
This is one of the greatest idle games out there, wether you used to play RuneScape or not this is definitely the option for anyone looking for a progress game that won’t consume hours of your time yet will give you great feelings of accomplishment when you reach your goals. 

I hope that updates continue to release for this game and the developer stays consistent. I feel like this will be even greater in time so staying up to date and playing everyday is making me excited for new content. 🙏🏼

reviews.title: Do you like RPGs and Idle Games?!
reviews.text: Then this is the game for you! Has a real RuneScape + idle vibe to it.  iPhone interface is a little cramped and unintuitive but if you start on a larger screen it will make more sense.  There’s a web app for that. And Melvore Cloud let’s you cross-play from your devices.  Love that the iPad app have both vertical and horizontal play, wish I could do split screen.  Game is a 5/5 for me (for the genre), app loses a star because it’s still very much under development and not the ideal way to play.

reviews.title: Best idle game I've tried
reviews.text:
I've played my fair share of games, and I especially like mobile idle games. This one is top-notch. All the skills, the offline progress, the variety. I actually get to choose which of the many things I want to work on. 

And the best part? No microtransactions. Just solid, uninterrupted gameplay.

Writing this review helped me realize how much time I've spent playing this quality game, and I'll be donating right after this. Immense thank you to the devs.

reviews.title: Very annoying bugs
reviews.text: Great game on PC, but this version is riddled with very annoying bugs, sometimes my offline progress doesn’t even register, I’ve had the game for a single day and so far took 2 fairly long breaks from playing, but both times the game didn’t register that any time had passed and didn’t give me the levels or resources it was supposed to. Another issue is that the game constantly thinks I’m offline while I’m in the app. When I’m trying to do things I’ve been spammed with offline notifications every time i gather a single resource. I want to recommend this game, and it is a fun game, but the bugs just make it far too frustrating for me to get invested in it.

reviews.title: good game bad ux
reviews.text: This game is good but could be much better if it had better ux. A lot of buttons and features seem to be laid out aimlessly without reason. Information stacked up on each other without the thought of importance and hierarchy. It seems that people typically would use the app with a bit of confusion until they get used to it which is one way to get past this terrible ux, but the only people who would stay are those who have played runescape before and mainly continue to play for that reason. Any newcomers that have not played runescape would not have an incentive to continue playing. Jagex: please hire a ux team.

reviews.title: Great OSRS Feeling
reviews.text: As someone who loves OSRS but has trouble finding the time to sink into it, finding a game like this was a wonderful surprise. I’ve been searching for a good idle RPG for a while now, and this is the best I’ve come across so far. It’s not pay to win, it’s consistent even though it’s in alpha, and it looks like the developers have barely scratched the surface with all the things they could do with this game in the future. I can’t wait to see how it evolves and I’m glad I found it early!

reviews.title: It really costs $10 but it’s worth every cent
reviews.text:
This is my favorite idol game I have ever played. It really scratches that itch perfectly imo. I never played OSRS but I never felt I was missing any of the “required reading”. That being said if you have played OSRS is that stripped down to its bare components and I love that. 

 There are a few things you should know before going in. 

-if you want to the full experience you will need to pay at least $10 (there are also expansions for a few extra bucks. I have Herald of the throne and I would say that and the base game are the essential experience)
-you are basically just initially downloading a demo, which I think is good because that way you can really see if you like this type of game. 
-this is a premium idle game. Fully polished. No micro-transactions or subscriptions after buying the full game.  
-once you’re in, be ready to bookmark the wiki. You’ll want that as I’m sure you’ll

reviews.title: 6/5 stars!!!
reviews.text: I have nothing but praise for this game! Everything about it reminds me of RS. I recommend it to anyone who is a fan of RS. I would also recommend it to anyone who is a fan of idle games but has no idea what I’m talking about when I say RS. I would give it 6/5 stars if I could. There are plenty of skills to work through, frequent updates (that are beneficial and not junk!), and the best part is, you can idle a lot of the skills but still need to be aware of what you’re doing and what to do next.

reviews.title: Excellent Game
reviews.text:
Melvor is undoubtedly the best idle game on the market. While based on RuneScape there are comprehensive guides for nearly any activity online easily accessible and there is never a moment wasted (unless you run out of resources for certain skills but that just requires attentiveness which creates an additional layer of game design) 

Overall the complexity of the game mixed with the “numbers go up” mentality our generation of gamers have, I truly believe Melvor Idle is one of the best games of its kind

reviews.title: “RuneScape Idle” 10/10
reviews.text: This game is amazing. It gives me all the nostalgia of RuneScape. Yes I know they have both versions on the App Store, but this is a whole new level. It has a clean interface and is fun to grind your levels and whatnot while doing other things and coming back. I’d love to see how this game further updates! Also my own little feedback is if there were sound effects, just small additions like that would really add a nice touch.

reviews.title: Great First Idle Game
reviews.text: I’d never played an idle game before but a friend of mine recommended that I try this after hearing I was burning out on OSRS (happens every few months) and I have been hooked since day 1. The game is obviously inspired by OSRS as the author says but it adds so much to the game and is so fascinating. I can play actively doing combat or training certain skills or can AFK woodcut for hours at a time. Would highly recommend if you’ve played OSRS and are looking for something similar!

reviews.title: Great work
reviews.text:
So far I haven’t been disappointed. Even though the game is still in alpha, the game has a solid foundation and seems to be making decent progress. Sure it may just be another idle game, but unlike other idle games, Melvor isn’t simply a click and wait app where you’re just waiting for your next upgrade with nothing to do but... wait. 

If you haven’t downloaded this game, try it!

As for The Dev team, keep up the great work. I look forward to seeing the future updates 🥰

reviews.title: This game used to be cool
reviews.text: Back when I played this game I want to say last year, there weren’t a lot of games like this and I really enjoyed playing it on the side of OSRS. But since they have updated the game they have gotten money hungry and locked out a lot of content for “premium players”. This would be fine if they didn’t have this content free to everyone before. Like how are you going to make this content free and then one day decide, “oh yeah, our game is doing pretty good, so let’s make some more money out of it and lock people out of content and force them to buy premium… genius”… honestly it would be a 5 star rating, but now, you guys look like a bunch of clowns.

reviews.title: Very fun, UI needs work
reviews.text: One of the most fun incremental games I’ve played in a while.  However, the interface is very often counter intuitive.  You can’t examine individual combat skills and how they might improve.  Nor is the game good at always letting you know conveniently when you might have a certain item.  Still, it’s early release and they have time to tweek those and similar issues.  Apart from only playing three days, I can’t seem to put it down.

reviews.title: Great game
reviews.text: I love how this game plays and really only have a few points that could be improved. One of which is the ability to choose how many of the item your making and maybe making a item that allows you to have an action list your character will follow. Lastly an auction house or something to buy and sell things to other players. Idk if you can call it a grand exchange but that would make it that much better. Other than that it’s a good game and scratch’s that runescape itch that I’ve had for a while.

reviews.title: The game is amazing but.....
reviews.text: The game is really fun and a great time killer it’s not pushy or pay to win like most idle games so already that super cool I like the direction they are going with visuals I looked forward to what else they have in mind I am really hoping for a multiplayer mode where you and your friends can team up to fight in the dungeons abs that mini game goblin rad is really fun and addictive but it pretty pointless to play right now I can’t wait for some kind of reward system anyways the game is awesome.

reviews.title: Not going idle
reviews.text: So I never read reviews but at this point I don’t want to play anymore. The point of the game is to be able to go idle. Recently every time I go away, I come back to seeing I’ve been inactive the whole time. I bought the full version and at higher levels, you need to much to actively play. Being able to idle farm is honestly what makes the game possible. I’m not sure if I’m doing something wrong or there’s a bug, but it’s ruined my whole experience.

reviews.title: Great, with a few hiccups
reviews.text:
Really scratches a similar itch to RuneScape, but in idle form. I love it. 
Some minor glitches though, and anytime your internet connection status changes you’ll get booted to the login screen and lose any recent changes you’ve made. Doesn’t sound too bad, but the number of times I’ve harvested, replanted, and sold all of my crops and changed training only to unexpectedly disconnect from or reconnect to WiFi and have to do everything again is a bit infuriating.

reviews.title: Simply the Best Idle game there is.
reviews.text: I’ve been playing this game in the background of my browser for a year now and I’m only 40% of the way through the wealth of content there is to unlock. It’s like an rpg that plays itself while leaving you interesting choices to make. Fantastic game. I just started a new character on mobile, and it is a different experience thanks to the order I chose to unlock things!

reviews.title: Download this game if you like RS
reviews.text: My friend told me to get this game and I was hesitant at first because idle games were never my cup of tea. I was absolutely shocked when I fell in love with this game right away. I experience Runescape nostalgia every time I open this app. This game is only in alpha and it’s already earned my complete support.  The developer communicates with his/her community and is very open to advice/suggestions from what I’ve seen.  So please download this game.  I want nothing but to see this game thrive.

reviews.title: Possibly the best idle game I’ve ever played!!
reviews.text: I love how the whole game is about skills that somehow interact with each other. There are a few problems but they’re minor enough. One problem I do have is the whole idle deal it’s not necessarily idle you have to completely shut down the game for it to actually be idle. Also, most of the other problems are things that deal with the combat. It’s messy but still great. I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys playing idle games

reviews.title: Not idling properly
reviews.text: I enjoy the game however when i close the app and have it running in the background it does not continue to progress even while connected to internet. Game fully continues upon reopening but immediately stops once closed again. I don know if this is normal because it actually does properly idle for certain skills but not all. Im pretty new and havent tried out all the available skills yet. Ive noticed it doesnt work for combat or cooking so far but does work for fishing woodcutting mining and smithing.

reviews.title: Amazing way to play runescape if you live a hectic life
reviews.text: I have a very busy day to day life with very little time to sit down and play runescape. Melvor allows me the sam satisfaction i used to get from runescape back in the day, except now i dont have to sit there and click all day. I check melvor when going to the bathroom at work and its always awesome to see how i have progressed and what new items i have gotten while away. Love this game.

reviews.title: Love the game but it needs work!
reviews.text:
Genuinely having a great time with this. Some of the menus could be reworked so when your scrolled down at the bottom of the page you don’t have to scroll back to the top to see the recipe, such as smithing items. 

I got a few different ideas that could be some improvements that would make the game even cooler just from rearranging the layouts of a few skills.

reviews.title: Very Enjoyable
reviews.text: I'm gonna be completely honest, I didn't expect much when I first downloaded the game. However I have been pleasantly surprised, I can see the love of a game I hold close to my heart. Which by the obvious assumption is RuneScape, and I find myself playing this almost as much as I played RuneScape as a kid, it's nostalgic and fresh. I hope the developer really does continue to put the love that is already shown in the product.

reviews.title: Wow! Not what I was expecting!
reviews.text: First off, I’ve never played any games like this. Ive had the idle games but never these “text?” games... loved RuneScape back in middle school and was excited to see it come to iOS, but just cant seem to make the time to play on top of being addicted to summoners war for 6 years and having a full time job. Can’t wait to see what comes in future updates and you have my support. ✌🏼

reviews.title: Shockingly Good
reviews.text:
I’ve never liked idle games before, but this actually feels like a real RPG. 
What really got me was the built in mod integration. BUILT-IN MOD INTEGRATION!! I never would have even thought that I’d want it, but now that I’ve experienced it, why doesn’t every ios game do that??

Thank you very much to the devs for creating this masterpiece, and thank you oh so much for making the full version a one-time payment!

reviews.title: Yikes
reviews.text: The beginning of the game has a “tutorial” that only tells you a task, BUT NOT HOW TO DO IT! You know how most mobile games basically control your screen for you and add arrows and text boxes to teach you? This game has NOTHING! It took me a few minutes to figure out where i was supposed to go to do the tasks and then what buttons to push and figure out how the UI worked. I was very confused with the setup of the game and having zero instructions didn’t help at all. I loves games like this one, but this is a terrible first impression and I don’t think I’ll be opening the app ever again.

reviews.title: Warning
reviews.text: I think that this game is a really great game and I have been playing it for around a month or two. If you get the game, beware that they recently made it so you have to pay $10 to unlock premium in order to unlock the rest of the skills. It isn’t as bad if you have been playing like I have though. I have a total level of 1076 but I can’t level up around half of the skills. I still think this is an amazing game even with that so yeah. That’s just a little heads up but you should get this game.

reviews.title: Fun game, but frustrating
reviews.text: Bought the game on my phone thinking I could play on a browser as well, but you don’t get access to the online version. You have to buy the $10 steam version too. I wish that information would have been available before I bought it. I would have bought the steam version instead.  I’ve been waiting patiently for information if it’s going to change, it sounds like an issue they’re working on. But no updates on it in 2 months.

reviews.title: Seriously the best free casual idle game I’ve seen in a while
reviews.text: In an age when most if not all mobile games are a cash grab with paywalls, this game has been such a blessing. There are some small UI and usability issues on mobile (compared to the desktop version) but this is all being made by one fantastic person and I’m not gonna nitpick. Bought the pc version and ad-free thing just to support the creator. What a gem.

reviews.title: Thank you so much for this game
reviews.text: I’ve been playing RuneScape since the original came out and now that I’m older I don’t have the time to play. This game has made me feel like a kid again!!! One thing I found a glitch to train multiple skills at once ( I’m honestly not sure how to recreate it which I know is not much help butttt, I thought I would say that it is possible and I do believe this is a bug.

reviews.title: An Idle RuneScape Game!!!
reviews.text: This is an amazing game! It’s almost just like RuneScape only idle! I love that you only pay premium $10 one time (I wish it was like on the regular RuneScape game). It would be great if the free skills at are like in the actual RuneScape game was the same for this game. Also it would be amazing if we could create our own character just like in RuneScape but in idle form. Please keep on updating this and make it as amazing as RuneScape

reviews.title: Still playing a year later
reviews.text: It’s been so cool to watch this game evolve. It’s very balanced and being able to be offline and still collect EXP and “explore” is great for those of us that can’t sit down with RuneScape for hours every day. The interface is easy to use and it’s put together very nicely. Aesthetically pleasing, plenty of content, and consistent offline progression make for a great little time killer.

reviews.title: Best idle game hands down
reviews.text: I’ve been playing RuneScape since 2003 on and off, this game is certainly different but obviously inspired by it. And it’s a one and done payment, no micro transactions. In classic RuneScape style, you get into one skill, then find yourself needing to train another, over and over. I love it. Bit buggy, but it’s the alpha version so I’m not worried. So far it’s been a blast. Can’t wait to see how it develops.

reviews.title: Wow it’s pretty good
reviews.text:
I don’t usually write reviews, but man I was looking for an idle game and this hit the spot. This game is in its early stages of development, but it already has enough for me to come back daily. The only thing I’d really want them to add is some audio. I don’t know how copyright works, but it would be awesome if you guys got some of the Osrs Soundtrack with some of the audio for skills and combat ~

Ad removal was like 3$, no problem at all lol

reviews.title: Love the game but one tweak.
reviews.text: This game is so much fun, especially if you love loot rpgs. The only problem I would have if they could make a system where you could organize your inventory. I would love it if they made it where you can create and name folders. For example I wish I could make a folder for my armor/weapons so I could put all my armor and weapons in a separate spot in my inventory. It can be really annoying having to look at a mess in my inventory. Other than that the game is solid.

reviews.title: Worth every expansion
reviews.text: People who don't have time to grind but can appreciate numbers going up and progress being made will love this game. It isn't mindless, every skill is unique and contributes to other skills due to skills needing each other. Township is an awesome feature that grows around your skills. Must try, strongly recommend buying the expansions.

reviews.title: Great game and concept but the bugs are so annoying
reviews.text: Specifically the bug where you load into a character and can’t do anything unless you close the app for 10 seconds and reopen it so you can click “ok” on your welcome back message. So very annoying and I’m considering stopping playing altogether specifically because of this bug. I’m tired of closing the app and reopening every single time I switch characters.

reviews.title: Fantastic Idle game
reviews.text: It has everything, so much QoL content for idle gamers with busy lives. I just started and feel like making a second character for a speed run is still an option. With future updates in the pipeline this is a must try, if you ask me. Based off of RuneScape with a mild learning curve, this will have your attention I promise.

reviews.title: Not sure why there is so much hate?
reviews.text: I’m all for supporting the developer if they stay active with the community and updates. I’ve bought the mobile version and steam. $20 dollars I spent in total isn’t nearly as bad as a RuneScape monthly sub or even their yearly, every game these days has a pay wall but if one time payment unlocks for lifetime then count me in.

reviews.title: Satisfying the need to master everything
reviews.text: I am very happy with the approach this game takes. The idea of having to manage a variety of inter-related resources and activities in order to craft things and build prowess appeals to my sense of progression. The interface is clean and reasonably uncluttered. I look forward to seeing what the devs have in mind for any future updates.

reviews.title: Great Until It Wasn’t
reviews.text:
Well, I was enjoying the game for quite awhile for the past 3 months, checking it every day and feeling satisfied about how I was mastering all of my skills and getting that satisfying gold “99” 
progression highlight in my menu.
 
Until the most recent update. 

If I would like to continue to progress any of my skills I must now pay $10 to have access to any of my previously progressed skills and I am stuck behind a baby-gate just like the original OSRS. 

The game was previously free on mobile and had cost $10 to purchase on the Steam store, but is now $10 to unlock the majority of the game on mobile as well.

 I would gladly pay $5 for this game.

I am disappointed, but it was fun while it lasted and I do applaud the developer in his work; however, the mobile game market is filled to the brim with other idle games.

reviews.title: Should be renamed to OSRS RIP-OFF PAYWALL IDLE. ALL OTHER REVIEWS ARE FAKE!!
reviews.text:
Over 75% of this game is blocked by a paywall. You can literally play through so much more OSRS than this plus have the ability to customize a Character, access to trivial things like prayer skill, explore, chat, and have a god tier community backing you up. This is the perfect example of GREEDY SELFISH App developers. I will find a way to report this game, it shouldn’t even have a free mode. I’ve seen the believable past reviews, especially the ones pointing out where the game used to be entirely FTP. Shame on this developer, shame on Apple for not vetting this stuff. 

SHUN THE LIARS!!

reviews.title: Addicting!
reviews.text: I have never played idle games before and despite my friends begging me to play RuneScape I never did. I decided to try Melvor Idle out and I have been hooked since. It’s simple to get started yet so much to do. I haven’t stopped playing for weeks. I am now attempting adventure mode with melee only as a personal challenge. This game is whatever u make it!

reviews.title: How I thought RuneScape mobile would look like!
reviews.text: Great little Idle game! Has a lot of resemblance to RuneScape and it’s very easy to jump into! There is a premium option, but the free options gives plenty to do before you decide if premium is for you. I’m excited Jagex got behind this game because it does pays homage to how RuneScape is played. Two thumbs up for me! 👍🏽👍🏽

reviews.title: Lvl 99 Idling
reviews.text: What can I say. This is a mobile port of the computer version of Melvor. The game is literally just the enjoyment of seeing those fat exp drops constantly. What is there not to look forward to playing in this game. I’m just saying if y’all don’t have 99 fletching, 99 crafting, 99 smithing, 99 woodcutting, 99 mining, and 99 runecrafting before you start combat training you doing something wrong with your life!

reviews.title: Amazing game
reviews.text: Hands down perfect for the Old School RuneScape players that don’t have the time to play anymore but still scratch that itch. The fact that it’s diverging is pretty cool and seems to be heading in an even greater direction. The UI can use a bit of work on iOS and there are a few bugs to work out but despite that, 5/5 game.

reviews.title: Enjoyable lasting fun.
reviews.text: I loved RuneScape but never had the time to stick with it.  Always yard work or work to do.  This allows me to actually level up without giving up due to lack of time.  I have already upgraded because of the fun and how it fits in with my real world schedule.  Even if I get all 99s I will keep going just for the fun of it.

reviews.title: Just like RuneScape!!!
reviews.text: Honestly I play this in between the down time of playing RuneScape. It has all the same skills but no paying barrier to get the “membership” skills. Also you can leave it woodcutting, mining, or fishing and come back and BAM. you have like 2k more ore, fish or wood plus all the exp. great game all around. Just wish it had something like a tutorial for harder skills like herblore and farming.

reviews.title: Best idle to date.  Yet offers a lot more.
reviews.text:
Coming from somebody whose been searching the app. Store extensively, and quite often since ~2016, and a hardcore gamer of 20+ years..  Melvor Idle is the real deal.

Amazing concept.  Single-player, yet heaps of insanely immersive and self driven, competitive fun.

The idle system in this game is hands down the best of any!  Just select a skill to harvest/function to perform, and close the App.  But things like combat, or thievery require a persons attentiveness in case you have to heal.  Even then, there’s rewards in the shop that can be purchased with in-game currency (there’s no other option for real life $) and let your character go automated to perform them.  Amongst a lot of other things 

Speaking of the shop, literally the only purchase with real $ in this game is to remove the advertisements for like $3.00 and that’s it!

The game is essentially/literally based off Runescape, y

reviews.title: Very fun, but..
reviews.text: This game is very fun and if you like RuneScape, you’ll love this game. I just wish you could interact with other players because it gets a little boring after you get 99 everything and you kill the bosses and get what you want. It’s like… now what? You can’t play with others, (trade, raid, chat, etc.) so it just gets a bit old after playing for a while.

reviews.title: Misleading Tutorial and pay to play
reviews.text:
Games starts on a forced tutorial trying to show the basic features. You can get stuck if your bank gets full since there is no mention of how to empty it but I figured it out to keep going. Upon completion you are given access to freely select what to do next only to find that most of the options, even some of the ones walked through in the tutorial are locked behind the “Full Version” that must be purchased.

Classic bait and switch…..

reviews.title: Amazing

reviews.title: Best idle game

reviews.title: Unplayable, crashes non-stop
reviews.text:
DO NOT BUY ON IOS

For at least six months now the app has been literally unplayable and crashes non-stop, even when not using mods. The same holds true for playing this in a normal browser like safari or firefox, it’s all of iOS and not just the app. This is a documented problem, not a whiny “review” from an ignorant dingus mad at video game.  

The devs have acknowledged it and have no idea what’s causing the crashes. They propose no solution and have no fix in the pipeline. The only potential solution is the upcoming offline client which they say will allow them to understand what’s crashing g and why, but there’s still no guarantee it’ll be fixed then. 

Do not buy on iOS. Buy on steam and even then you won’t be able to play on iOS for the foreseeable future. It’s absolutely ridiculous.

reviews.title: Numbers go up

reviews.title: My Favorite Game!

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text:
As many others have written, as well as the title for this review, this game is an amazing idle rpg. 

I’ve never been one for text-based games such as this, being minimal with illustrations. However, this game had completely blown away my expectations. 

I started off with just the free version, after the tutorial I saw what was locked and I desperately wanted to use those skills. 

Personally, for the amount of time I’ve put into this game, mixed with the anticipation of leveling up locked skills, $10.00 is a small price to pay. 

Hours upon hours of content, getting deeper and more complex the more time you spend. 

I greatly appreciate the active support and updates, easily accessible wiki’s, news, and changelogs. (Straight from within the app) 

It makes it feel as if the developer truly cares about the player’s experience.
